candidate_relations.reason: The histological features described—polygonal to spindle-shaped cells forming nests within dilated sinusoids, narrow erythrocyte-containing spaces between tumor cells, vascular invasion, and a reticular fiber network on silver/Azan staining—are characteristic of hemangiosarcoma (endothelial origin), not hepatocellular carcinoma. Although clear cell morphology is mentioned in C001, the architectural pattern (sinusoidal growth, vascular channels, reticular stroma) and the reference diagnosis both point to a vascular tumor. HCC would show trabecular or acinar patterns with hepatocyte differentiation markers, not the vascular channel formation seen here.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Hepatocellular carcinoma is a hepatocyte-derived malignancy; hemangiosarcoma is an endothelial/vascular malignancy

case_quality_flags: Rat model context (Sprague-Dawley, 7 weeks) is consistent with spontaneous or induced hepatic hemangiosarcoma in rodent toxicology studies
Silver and Azan staining findings are key discriminators favoring vascular/endothelial origin over hepatocellular origin
